title: Choose the visual world for Wayfinder (web) — safer hand
question: Familiar directions, as requested. Pick one, or take the category standard.

options.label: Topographic Sheet
options.thesis: The app as a well-made national topo map: calm terrain tints, a collar with legend and scale, and a sheet index that fills in as you explore.
options.viewport: Map fills the screen inside a thin collar; a side panel reads like the legend panel, listing fastest and explore routes with minutes and new km.
options.risk: Earthy map palette is familiar and calm, and could feel plain if the collar details are skipped.

options.label: Street Directory
options.thesis: A dense, trusty directory: grid references, bold index tabs and a route plan that reads like a page of directions.
options.viewport: Map page with grid-reference margins; a tabbed index panel on the left for Plan, Discover, Coverage, Trips.
options.risk: Strong nostalgia for Australians; road-directory yellow can feel dated if overused.

options.label: National Park Signage
options.lineage: NPWS track signs and the Australian Walking Track Grading System
options.thesis: Routed-timber trail signs: clear distances, times and grades, with explore routes graded by how much new ground they cover.
options.viewport: Full map; route choices stacked like a trailhead signpost: destination, km, minutes, grade of newness.
options.risk: Very outdoorsy; driving-first users may find the trail framing a stretch.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Google Maps / Apple Maps / Organic Maps grammar: floating search, side panel of route cards, blue route line — executed at their craft level.
canonCard.viewport: Left panel with search and route cards over a full-screen map; explore routes as alternates with a 'new km' badge.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps it sits alongside, by design.
